correctness.rationale: PASS. Haar displacement is uniform in a fundamental Voronoi polygon V, so F(r)=area(V∩B_r)/area(V), with F(r)=πr²/A at small r. Direct polar differentiation yields F'(r)=r(2π-L(r))/A, where L is the union length of forbidden angular arcs from genuine facets. The perpendicular foot of each relevant Voronoi edge is interior, hence its pair of newborn arcs is isolated. For k opposite facet-pairs at distance d the one-sided derivative difference equals -4k sqrt(2d)/A sqrt(ε)+O(ε); mergers of previously existing arcs have locally bounded endpoint velocities and produce only O(ε). The number and multiplicities of recovered support distances are complete: two for an orthogonal rank-two basis; three for u,v,v-u when the Gauss-reduced inner product is positive. Lengths 2a,2b and polarization u·v=2(a²+b²-c²) determine the Gram matrix, including ties. Independently reconstructed forbidden-angular-arc lengths for three test shapes gave the correct sqrt multiplicity. A finite test does not establish the inverse theorem, which follows from the explicit geometric argument.
